maya: Ran a quick cross-cloud microbench for A100 80GB (batch=1, seq=512) to compare driver/CUDA stack effects. TL;DR: Azure node shows tail-latency hysteresis after driver toggles, much worse p99 spikes than AWS/GCP.

maya: Raw numbers (1k inferences each, warmup 200):
- AWS p4d (driver 525.60.11, CUDA 12.1): p50=30ms p95=120ms p99=220ms
- GCP a2 (driver 525.85, CUDA 11.8): p50=28ms p95=90ms p99=180ms
- Azure ND96 (driver 525.60, CUDA 12.1): p50=31ms p95=300ms p99=900ms (spikes clustered, not steady)

kevin: Can you paste the exact command and model config? curious about KV cache warmup and quant flags.

maya: Sure, command used:
```
./bench_infer --model redwood-v1-7b-quant --batch 1 --seq 512 --warmup 200 --iter 1000 --quant int4 --kernels auto
```
Also ran a variant with `--kernels cublaslt` and saw slightly lower medians but Azure still had outliers.

perf-bot: Dashboard uploaded: https://grafana.internal/d/bench/cross-cloud-a100/1794301123 (charts: latency timeline, p50/p95/p99, throughput) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

aiden: Two quick hypotheses: 1) Azure NIC or PCIe rescan during kernel JIT triggers GC-like pauses on certain driver builds; 2) different cuBLAS/cuBLASLt minor versions cause different kernel selection for int4 paths -> different launch latencies.

sophie: I've seen similar with quant kernels — the int4 kernels on some stacks fall back to a multi-stage kernel that allocates temp buffers, which can trigger host syncs. That would explain p99s but not median. Also suspect memory fragmentation after our persistent allocation pattern.

kevin: Did you check driver logs / dmesg on the Azure nodes? any GPU reset or nv-hostengine messages?

maya: Quick grep showed repeated warnings around timestamp range on Azure: `nvidia: channel 'nv-hostengine' reported event` and occasional `NVRM: GPU lockup - aborting`. Not full resets but correlates with spikes.

kevin: Hmm. Could be firmware mismatch between ND96 image and AMD host firmware + driver. Worth trying 525.85 (GCP match) on Azure image or downgrading CUDA compat.

aiden: Also try forcing kernel selection: export `XLA_FLAGS`? for our runtime we have a flag `--force-cublaslt` and `--disable-persistent-kernel`. Run both permutations:
```
./bench_infer --model ... --quant int4 --kernels cublaslt --disable-persistent-kernel
./bench_infer --model ... --quant int4 --kernels jit --persistent-kernel
```
Collect per-iteration latencies and nvprof/cupti traces for the spike window.

sophie: For capacity sizing: given Azure p99 volatility, plan +20-30% spare capacity for Dedicated pools in that region until we have a driver/kernel fix. Otherwise clients hit SLA blips.

maya: Agreed. I'll re-run the cross-stack matrix tonight with these permutations and upload traces. Next steps: 10m steady-state runs, enable `nvidia-smi dmon`, collect `dmesg` and `libnvidia` logs, and try driver 525.85 on Azure image.

kevin: Great. If you capture a short flamegraph of CPU/GPU-side stalls we can decide whether to fallback to GCP for critical workloads.

perf-bot: Created tracking ticket INF-9723 with the basic bench artifacts link and labels `cross-cloud`, `driver-hysteresis`, `quant-int4`. :spiral_note_pad:

sophie: Thanks — ping me when traces are up, I'll run kernel symbol diff and kernel launch histograms. :thumbsup:

maya: Will do. Thanks team.
